title: Representation Invariance and Allocation: When Subgroup Balance Matters

bias_targets.methodology: Varying the allocation of male vs. female samples (or mention vs. no mention of gender) during model fine-tuning and measuring subgroup-specific performance changes (accuracy, loss, AUC) in medical imaging (MIMIC-CXR, HAM10000) and text classification (Civil_comments).

Varying the allocation of training data based on racial groups (e.g., White vs. Non-White in MIMIC-CXR, or race mentions in Civil_comments) and evaluating the impact on subgroup test performance and correlating it to latent space separation.

Fine-tuning models on datasets with varying proportions of age subgroups (e.g., under/above 60 in MIMIC-CXR, under/above 50 in HAM10000) to assess how subgroup representation affects predictive accuracy and loss.
Adjusting the representation of comments mentioning religion in the Civil_comments dataset during fine-tuning to observe the effect on subgroup generalization.
Varying the training allocation of text samples mentioning sexual orientation in the Civil_comments dataset and tracking subsequent model performance on that subgroup.
Evaluating model performance sensitivity to the proportion of English vs. Non-English speaking patient records in the MIMIC-CXR dataset during training.
Using patient insurance type (Private vs. Not-private) in the MIMIC-CXR dataset as a proxy for socioeconomic subgroup, varying its training allocation, and measuring the resulting predictive parity.
Varying the allocation of married vs. unmarried patient records in the MIMIC-CXR training data to evaluate subgroup performance sensitivity.
